verses.71:3: {suscipiant} os montes a paz para o povo: * e as colinas, a justiça.

verses.71:6: Descerá como a chuva sobre {vellus}: * e como gotas que gotejam sobre a terra.
verses.71:7: {orietur} nos seus dias a justiça, e a abundância da paz: * até que a lua seja tirada.
verses.71:8: E dominará de mar a mar: * e desde o rio até {terminos} do mundo.
verses.71:9: Os etíopes se prostrarão diante dele: * e os seus inimigos {lingent}.
verses.71:10: Os reis de Társis e as ilhas oferecerão {m10}: * os reis dos árabes e de Sabá {adducent} {d10}.
verses.71:11: E o adorarão todos os reis da terra: * todas as nações o servirão:
verses.71:12: Porque livrará o pobre do poderoso: * e o pobre que não tinha {adjutor}.
verses.71:13: {parcet}: * e salvará as almas dos pobres.

verses.71:15: E viverá, e lhe será dado do ouro da Arábia, {deipso}: * o dia todo o bendirão.

decisions.why: The verse sets *in justítia … in judício* side by side (ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ … ἐν κρίσει). *judícium → juízo* is settled (D15). *com justiça* is the psalter's form for *judicáre … in justítia* (9:8b *julgará os povos com justiça*). The second member cannot take the same preposition: *julgar com juízo* is heard in Brazil as 'judge sensibly' (*ter juízo*). *em juízo* is what Ps 9:8b ruled for *in judício* (the Latinist's major there; 118:154 too): the Latin's preposition, and the court sense a Brazilian hears in it is the verse's own. MS1932 *com equidade* is another word (*æquitas*).

options.label: em juízo
options.note: Ruling; 9:8b's wording for *in judício*.

options.label: com juízo
options.note: the same preposition twice, as the Latin has it; but *com juízo* is heard as 'sensibly'.

options.label: no juízo
options.note: to the letter (1:5, 24:9); here it can be heard as 'at the Judgment'.

decisions.why: The *suscípere* (a thing as object) row is open with *acolher* and names this verse: D19's *amparar* is built on persons, and *amparem a paz* would prop peace up. The Greek is ἀναλαβέτω, 'take up, receive'. DRB 'receive', MS1932 *Recebam*. *Acolher* keeps the row; *receber* is plainer, but it is the word for *accípere* (which the psalter has often), and the row keeps *suscípere* apart from it.

options.label: Acolham
options.note: Ruling; the suscípere (thing) row.

options.label: Recebam
options.note: MS1932, DRB 'receive'; merges suscípere with accípere.

decisions.latin: et ante lunam … ante solem pérmanet nomen ejus
decisions.why: *ante* (πρό) is both place and time: 'in the presence of' and 'earlier than'. Portuguese must choose: *diante de* is place, *antes de* is time. In 71:5 the pair *cum sole, et ante lunam* says how long the king lasts — as long as the sun, in the sight of the moon — and 'earlier than the moon' does not fit a future; MS1932 turns it *tanto como o sol e a lua*. In 71:17 *ante solem pérmanet nomen ejus* could be either, and MS1932 chooses time (*o seu nome existe antes do sol*, a reading the Christian use of the psalm welcomes). The Latin uses one word in both verses, and one Portuguese word keeps the echo: ruled *diante* in both, which reads the second verse as the first is read. The time reading of 71:17 stays one touch away.

options.label: diante … diante
options.note: Ruling; one word for one word in both verses; place.

options.label: diante … antes
options.note: MS1932's reading of 71:17 (time: the name before the sun); breaks the echo with 71:5.

options.label: perante … perante
options.note: the same sense as the ruling, more formal.

decisions.why: *vellus* is a fleece (L&S: wool shorn off, the fell with the wool on it; πόκος). *Velo* is the Portuguese word (MS1932), the fleece of Gideon (Judges 6, where Portuguese Bibles have *velo* — not checked here), and the image the Church has read of the Incarnation. It may be unknown to some hearers. *lã* (the plain word) loses the fleece for the wool. The Hebrew's mown grass (DM1962 *relva*) is not the Latin. **v2:** the stylist called *velo* bookish and the ambiguity reader listed it as unknown, hearing *véu* or *velho*: a wrong first hearing. *a lã* keeps the wool, the concrete thing the rain falls on; the fleece as a whole is lost. *o velo* stays option 2. **Gate (v2):** the Latinist asked *o velo* back (minor: *lã* is the material, not the fleece). Held: the ambiguity reader did not know *velo* and heard *véu* or *velho* — a wrong first hearing weighs more than the loss of the whole hide, and the rain on wool still stands. *o velo* stays option 2 for whoever rules.

options.label: a lã
options.note: Ruling (v2); stylist and ambiguity reader.

options.label: o velo
options.note: Draft 1; the Latin's fleece, MS1932; unknown to the ambiguity reader.

decisions.why: *oríri* (ἀνατέλλω) is the rising of a heavenly body and the springing of a plant; the verse is an Advent versicle (Adv1-1, Adv3-0, Adv3-3, grep), where justice rises as a sun. *Nascer* says both — the sun is born (*o nascer do sol*, 49:1) and plants are born — and is plain. *Surgir* keeps the rising and loses the plant. MS1932 *aparecerá* is flatter than the Latin's image. No row yet; proposed as *oríri → nascer* (open).

options.label: Nascerá
options.note: Ruling; sunrise and sprouting both.

options.label: Surgirá
options.note: the rising only.

options.label: Aparecerá
options.note: MS1932; drops the image.

decisions.why: The *términi terræ* row keeps *os limites* for *términi* and *confins* for *fines*, but Ps 64:8 took *os confins* for *términos* alone because the Greek is πέρατα there as in 64:6 (D15's test), after the stylist heard *os limites* as administrative and the blind reader as frontiers. Here the Greek is again πέρατα τῆς οἰκουμένης — the same Greek as 18:5 *in fines orbis terræ* → *até os confins do mundo*. So *confins*, and the colon ends as 18:5 does. *orbis terrárum → o mundo* (D30).

options.label: os confins
options.note: Ruling; 64:8, 18:5 (same Greek).

options.label: os limites
options.note: the row's working word for términi (2:8); keeps términi and fines apart.

decisions.why: The Latin's image is licking the ground (λείξουσιν; the Greek has χοῦν, 'dust'). Concrete images stay (rule 5). MS1932 *beijarão a terra* softens it into a gesture of homage, which the Latin does not say.

options.label: lamberão a terra
options.note: Ruling; the Latin's verb and noun.

options.label: beijarão a terra
options.note: MS1932; another image.

options.label: lamberão o pó
options.note: the Greek's χοῦν; not the Latin's *terram*.

decisions.why: The *múnera* row (open) is *dádivas* and names this verse (and 67:30 *os reis vos oferecerão dádivas*, the same kings' gifts). *dona* has no row; the Greek has δῶρα for both, so D15 would allow one word — but the Latin varies, Portuguese has a plain pair, and one word would make the two colons say *dádivas … dádivas*. *presentes* is the row's option for *múnera*; here it takes *dona*. The verse is the Epiphany's (versicle, antiphon, responsories, Offertory — Sancti/01-06, grep). **v2:** the stylist asked *dons* (the proparoxytone *dádivas* at the mediant). Held for the múnera row, as at 44:13 against the same objection; *dons* is now option 3 with *presentes* kept for *dona*. The ambiguity reader listed *dádivas* as unknown.

options.label: dádivas … presentes
options.note: Ruling; múnera row; dona → presentes (proposed, open).

options.label: presentes … dons
options.note: MS1932 has *dons … presentes*, the other way round.

options.label: dons … presentes
options.note: the stylist's; an oxytone at the mediant.

decisions.why: *addúcere → levar* is settled (D42; 42:3, 44:15b–16 *Serão levadas ao Rei*). *Trazer* is the word a Portuguese speaker reaches for with gifts (MS1932 *trarão*), but it is the word of *afférre* (28:1–2 *Afférte Dómino → Trazei ao Senhor*, 95:7), which the row keeps apart. *levar presentes* is plain Portuguese. **v2:** the Latinist (minor) asked *trarão*: *addúcere* is bringing toward. Held for the row (D42): *levar presentes* to a king is movement toward him in Portuguese too, and *trazer* is kept for *afférre*. **Gate (v2):** the same minor repeated (*trarão*); held for D42 as in v1.

options.label: levarão
options.note: Ruling; the addúcere row (D42).

options.label: trarão
options.note: MS1932; merges addúcere with afférre.

decisions.latin: et páuperem, cui non erat adjútor
decisions.why: The *adjútor* row (open, for Gustavo) is *auxílio* in every finished place. Here it is the most natural it has been: *não tinha auxílio* is how Portuguese says it. The agent noun *auxiliador*, which the Latinist has asked for elsewhere, is the option; MS1932 turns it into a clause (*quem lhe valha*). **v2:** the Latinist and the stylist both asked for the person (*quem o ajudasse*): *adjútor* is a helper, and *não tinha auxílio* made him an abstraction. Taken in the row's own verb (*adjuváre → auxiliar*, 43:26 *auxiliai-nos*): a noun turned into a clause is grammar (D2) and keeps the person. This departs from the row's uniform *auxílio*, which is still open for Gustavo; the build is local — there is no *meus* here and no pairing with another agent noun.

options.label: quem o auxiliasse
options.note: Ruling (v2); the Latinist and stylist, in the row's verb (they wrote *ajudasse*, which is *adjuváre* in another word).

options.label: auxílio
options.note: Draft 1; the adjútor row's uniform word; both readers heard an abstraction.

options.label: auxiliador
options.note: the agent noun, as the Latin's.

decisions.why: The *párcere* row (open) is *poupar* and names this verse (18:13 *poupai o vosso servo*). φείσεται is 'spare, have pity on'. *Poupar o pobre* is heard as 'spare' — faithful, though it can suggest the poor were due a blow. MS1932 *Usará de clemência com*; *ter compaixão* is plainer but is not the verb of *miseréri* (*ter piedade*) only by a hair. *inops → carente* (D38). **v2:** the stylist asked *necessitado* for *carente* ('social-work vocabulary'). Refused: D38 settles *inops → carente*, and *necessitado* is *egénus*'s, reserved.

options.label: Poupará

forms.parcet: Poupará o pobre e o carente

options.note: Ruling; the párcere row.

options.label: Terá compaixão

forms.parcet: Terá compaixão do pobre e do carente

options.note: the sense of φείδομαι as pity; near miseréri's *ter piedade*.

options.label: Será clemente

forms.parcet: Será clemente com o pobre e o carente

options.note: after MS1932 *usará de clemência*.

decisions.latin: et honorábile nomen eórum coram illo
decisions.why: The colon has no verb; the tense of the psalm is future (DRB 'shall be honourable'). A copula is grammar (D2). *honorábilis* is 'worthy of honour, held in honour'; *será honrado* says it plainly (MS1932 *será em honra*). *eórum* → *deles*, so that it is not heard as the king's (*o seu*), as in the first colon. **v2:** the Latinist: *honorábile* is an adjective, 'worthy of honour', not the participle — taken as *digno de honra*. He also called the future supplied; held: the copula must have a tense, the psalm's verbs around it are future, and DRB supplies 'shall be'. The first colon now says *as suas almas* (the stylist: *deles … deles … dele* clattered, and the mediant *deles* chimed with the final *dele*); the possessive is heard as the poor's, whose souls these are in 71:13.

options.label: será digno de honra

forms.hon14: e o nome deles será digno de honra diante dele

options.note: Ruling (v2); the Latinist's sense of the adjective.

options.label: será honrado

forms.hon14: e o nome deles será honrado diante dele

options.note: Draft 1; the participle, 'honoured'.

options.label: verbless

forms.hon14: e honrado o nome deles diante dele

options.note: the Latin's ellipsis kept.

decisions.why: The hardest phrase of the psalm. The Greek is προσεύξονται περὶ αὐτοῦ, 'they shall pray concerning / for him'; the Latin renders the verb *adoráre*, whose old sense is 'entreat, pray' (L&S), and keeps *de*: 'concerning him'. DRB 'for him they shall always adore'; MS1932 drops the preposition, *e o adorarão sempre* — making him the object, as 71:11 *adorábunt eum*. The Latin keeps the two apart (*eum* / *de ipso*). *e por ele adorarão sempre* keeps the verb of 71:11 (a repetition the Latin has) and a preposition as open as *de*: 'for him', 'for his sake'. **v2:** the stylist found *por ele adorarão* hard to parse and moved *sempre* forward — taken (order). The Latinist passed the phrase and named it among the Septuagintal readings kept. The ambiguity reader heard 'adore him' first, 'pray for him' and 'through him' second — the openness of *de ipso* is heard.

options.label: e sempre adorarão por ele
options.note: Ruling; verb and preposition kept; v2 order from the stylist (*sempre* first, *por ele* after the verb).

options.label: e por ele adorarão sempre
options.note: Draft 1 order; the stylist found it hard to parse.

options.label: e o adorarão sempre
options.note: MS1932; drops *de*, so that it repeats 71:11.

options.label: e sempre orarão por ele
options.note: the Greek's sense; loses the Latin's verb.

decisions.why: D31 left 71:16 to be decided here. The word is not the sky here, and not God as a stay (D31's *esteio*): it is στήριγμα, 'a support', which in the Greek Bible is also the staff of bread (104:16 *omne firmaméntum panis*). DRB keeps 'firmament'; MS1932 reads *mantimento*, food. Portuguese *sustento* holds both senses the word carries here — what holds up and what feeds — without choosing between them. *firmamento* would be heard as the sky (D31). **v2:** the Latinist (minor): *sustento* is heard first as food, which slides to the Hebrew's grain; the ambiguity reader confirmed it ('food/sustenance'). Taken: *esteio*, D31's word for the prop, is the Latin's support (στήριγμα) without the food — the staff-of-bread sense needs *panis*, as at 104:16, which this verse does not have. *esteio* was unknown to one blind reader in Ps 17; it is the settled word.

options.label: esteio
options.note: Ruling (v2); the Latinist; D31's word for a support.

options.label: sustento
options.note: Draft 1; support and food both — heard as food first by the Latinist and the ambiguity reader.

options.label: mantimento
options.note: MS1932; only the food.

options.label: firmamento
options.note: DRB, the cognate; heard as the sky.

decisions.why: The *summus* row (open; 18:6b *extremo*) notes that at 71:16 'the tops of the mountains' — *cimo* fits there. *nos cumes* keeps the Latin's plural and is plainer than *cimo*; MS1932 *no cume*.

options.label: nos cumes dos montes
options.note: Ruling; the plural kept.

options.label: no cimo dos montes
options.note: the row's note.

options.label: no alto dos montes
options.note: plainest.

decisions.why: The verb has no expressed subject: *florébunt de civitáte* (ἐξανθήσουσιν ἐκ πόλεως) is 'they shall flower out of the city' — those of the city, or they, springing from it. DRB and MS1932 supply 'they of the city' / *os da cidade* (MS1932's note: the inhabitants of the messianic kingdom). Supplying the subject closes what the Latin leaves open; *e da cidade florescerão* keeps the Latin's build. **v2:** the ambiguity reader heard exactly the Latin's openness ('they will flourish from the city', without knowing who). Kept.

options.label: da cidade florescerão
options.note: Ruling; the Latin's openness kept.

options.label: os da cidade florescerão
options.note: DRB, MS1932; the subject supplied.

decisions.why: 36:2 has *fænum → feno* (*como o feno, depressa secarão*); rule 6 keeps it. Here the grass flowers, which hay does not do, and the Greek is χόρτος, 'grass'; MS1932 *a erva dos campos*. Held for the one Latin word; *erva* is the option, and if it is taken 36:2 should be looked at too. **v2:** the stylist ('hay does not flower, the image jars') and the ambiguity reader (*feno* unknown; heard as dry, short-lived) both refused *feno* here. Taken: a wrong image is a fault (rule 5), and the Greek is χόρτος, grass. 36:2 keeps *feno*, where the point is that it dries — so one Latin word has two Portuguese words, by what the verse does with it (as D32 splits *semen*). Proposed to the fænum row.

options.label: a erva
options.note: Ruling (v2); stylist and ambiguity reader; χόρτος; MS1932 *erva*.

options.label: o feno
options.note: Draft 1; 36:2's word; hay does not flower.

decisions.latin: Et benedicéntur in ipso omnes tribus terræ
decisions.why: *benedícere* God → man is open with *bendizer* (133:3, 28:11, 27:9, 66:2, 66:7b). The passive here is the promise to Abraham (*benedicéntur in te omnes cognatiónes terræ*, from memory, not checked). Kept in the row's verb, so the psalm's *benedíctum … benedicéntur … Benedíctus … benedíctum* (71:17–19) is one word, as the Latin has it. MS1932 *benditas*. The promise-formula wording was quoted from memory, unverified.

options.label: benditas
options.note: Ruling; the row; MS1932.

options.label: abençoadas
options.note: the everyday verb (DM1962); breaks the psalm's one word.

decisions.why: *solus* as a predicate: 'who alone does wonders'. DRB 'who alone doth', MS1932 *é só ele que faz*. *sozinho* would lean to 'without help'. *só ele* before the verb is the Portuguese of it. *mirabília → maravilhas* (9:2, 25:7).

options.label: que só ele faz maravilhas
options.note: Ruling.

options.label: que faz maravilhas sozinho
options.note: the Latin's order; leans to 'unaided'.

options.label: o único que faz maravilhas
options.note: after DM1962 *único que faz prodígios*.

decisions.latin: et replébitur majestáte ejus omnis terra
decisions.why: The replére (passive) row keeps the Latin's passive (*ser cheio*: 64:5b, 64:10b, 64:12). The stylist called *será cheia* a flat passive and asked the reflexive *se encherá* (MS1932 *encher-se-á*). Held for the row: the reflexive makes the earth fill itself, the passive says it is filled by another, as the Latin does. Option.

options.label: será cheia
options.note: Ruling; the replére row.

options.label: se encherá
options.note: the stylist; MS1932.

choices.71:2: The Latin's colon ends on the imperative (*regi da*); Portuguese order puts it first. *Deus* bare vocative (the row). *dai* is safe under rule 3 (*dei* ≠ *dai*). *judícium → juízo* (D15). The verse ends with a colon, as the Latin, because 71:2b depends on it.
choices.71:2b: *Judicáre* (the infinitive of purpose or result, κρίνειν) → *Para julgar*. *com justiça* as 9:8b.
choices.71:3: *pópulo* dative → *para o povo*. *colles → colinas* (64:13). The second colon verbless, as the Latin.
choices.71:4: *salvos fáciet → salvará* (salvum fácere row). *calumniátor → caluniador* (calumniári row, which names 71:4).
choices.71:5: *in generatióne et generatiónem → de geração em geração* (formula row; 32:11 has the same ablative form). *cum sole* kept literally (*com o sol*): the king lasts alongside the sun.
choices.71:6: *stillicídia stillántia* → *gotas que gotejam*: the Latin's figure of one root twice, kept (stillicídium row, *gota*).
choices.71:7: Advent versicle (Adv1-1, Adv3-0, Adv3-3). *abundántia → abundância* (row). *auferri → ser tirado* (auferre row, D41).
choices.71:8: *a mari usque ad mare → de mar a mar*, the Portuguese idiom; the second pair keeps *desde … até*. *orbis terrárum → o mundo* (D30). The Latin is a versicle and Alleluia (Adv2-0; 10-DU).
choices.71:9: *prócidere → prostrar-se* (no row; proposed, open). *Æthíopes → os etíopes*, the people's name in lower case as Portuguese writes it. **v2:** subject first, *coram illo* after the verb (the stylist): draft 1 put the proparoxytone *etíopes* at the mediant; order is grammar (D2). The ambiguity reader could take *os seus inimigos* as the Ethiopians' — as the Latin *ejus* can be; left.
choices.71:10: *Tharsis → Társis* (D43). *Árabum → dos árabes* (the Latin names the people; MS1932 *da Arábia* the land). *Reges Tharsis, et ínsulæ*: the islands are a second subject, as the Greek αἱ νῆσοι.
choices.71:11: The Latin's order (verb, then subject) kept: subject-first (*E todos os reis da terra o adorarão*) put *adorarão* at the mediant against *servirão* at the end, a rhyme the Latin does not have (checks). Each colon is said alone: the Epiphany Offertory's second half, an Advent versicle (Adv3-3), 10-DU.
choices.71:12: The Latin repeats *páuperem* (the Greek varies πτωχὸν … πένητα): the repetition is kept. *erat* → *não tinha* (the imperfect). No comma before *que*: the restrictive reading is the plainer one in Portuguese.
choices.71:13: *ánimas páuperum salvas fáciet → salvará as almas dos pobres*. The verse and 71:12 are the Epistle-verse of St Peter Claver (09-09n, aliquibus locis).
choices.71:14: *usúra → usura* (row, names this verse); the plural kept — unknown to the ambiguity reader, kept for the reproach the row wants. *rédimet → resgatará* (redímere row). **v2:** first colon *as suas almas* for *as almas deles* (stylist); *eórum* in the second colon stays *deles*, apart from the king's *dele*.
choices.71:15: *dábitur ei de auro* → *lhe será dado do ouro* (the partitive *de* kept). *tota die → o dia todo* (D24). *benedícent ei* → *o bendirão* (the dative made direct, as the benedícere row allows for pronouns).
choices.71:16: One long first colon with no flex in the Latin; the comma kept. *superextollétur super Líbanum* → *acima do Líbano se erguerá* (extóllere → erguer, row open; the *super-* of the verb carried by *acima*). The Latin's order puts *fructus ejus* last before the mediant; kept, so the colon closes on *fruto*. **v2:** comma after *na terra* (the stylist: two locatives ran together).
choices.71:17: *in sǽcula → pelos séculos* (D43, names 71:17). *nomen ejus* twice, kept.
choices.71:17b: *magnificáre → engrandecer* (row; the Greek μακαριοῦσιν, 'call blessed', is another verb — the Latin followed). *omnes tribus terræ → todas as tribos da terra*.
choices.71:18: The close of Book II. *Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël* → *Bendito o Senhor, Deus de Israel*, verbless, as 40:14 (D41). Responsory R. of Pent01-0 and Gradual of Epi1-0a (with *magna*, grep).
choices.71:19: *in ætérnum → para sempre* (D23). *replébitur → será cheia* (the replére row: passive kept). *fiat, fiat → assim seja, assim seja* (D41). The first colon verbless, carrying on 71:18's acclamation.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from the parallels (Latin, Rahlfs, WLC, DRB, MS1932, DM1962). Hard readings: 71:15 *adorábunt de ipso* (the old sense of adoráre, 'pray'; the Greek προσεύξονται περί), 71:16 *firmaméntum* (στήριγμα, support and staff of bread; D31 left it here), 71:16 *florébunt de civitáte* (no subject), 71:5 / 71:17 *ante* (place or time). Liturgical uses by grep (ps032/uses.py): Epiphany (71:10–11; Sancti/01-06 horas and missa), Advent (71:7, 71:8, 71:11; Adv1-1, Adv2-0, Adv3-0, Adv3-3), Epi1-0a (71:18 with *magna … a sǽculo*, 71:3 with *tuo*), Pent01-0 (71:18), 10-DU (71:8, 71:11), St Peter Claver (71:12–13). Glossary applied: D15 juízo, D23, D24, D30, D38, D41, D42, D43; rows suscípere (thing), términi, múnera, párcere, usúra, redímere, firmaméntum, summus, fænum (36:2), benedícere, adjútor, replére, stillicídium, calumniári, abundántia, magnificáre, majéstas.

Hard checks pass. Soft flags accepted: 71:5 second colon −6 (*de geração em geração*, the formula row; the Latin's doubled noun is in it) and first colon +3 (*diante da lua*); 71:8 first colon −5 (*de mar a mar*, the idiom for *a mari usque ad mare*; nothing omitted); 71:19 second colon +6 (*assim seja, assim seja*, D41, as 40:14); 71:4, 71:7 −3/+3 and 71:9, 71:10 +3 (Portuguese articles and the analytic *se prostrarão*, *seja tirada*). The rhyme flagged in draft 0 at 71:11 (*adorarão / servirão*) was removed by returning to the Latin's order. No cadence on a proparoxytone except 71:9 *etíopes*, 71:10 *dádivas*, 71:17 *séculos* at the mediant, where the Latin too is proparoxytone.
